project: Task 3 - published statistical evidence on smartphone use and sleep quality

primary_source.citation: Siebers, T., Beyens, I., Baumgartner, S. E., & Valkenburg, P. M. (2024). Adolescents’ Digital Nightlife: The Comparative Effects of Day- and Nighttime Smartphone Use on Sleep Quality. Communication Research.

data_method: Published aggregate statistics transcribed from article Tables 1-4. These are not participant-level records.

secondary_source.name: MMASH - Multilevel Monitoring of Activity and Sleep in Healthy People
secondary_source.description: Separate physiological dataset containing TST, WASO, awakenings, PSQI, activity and stress measures. Not merged into primary analysis.

limitations: Primary study participants are adolescents aged 13-16, not university students.
Primary study uses a 1-7 daily sleep diary item, not full PSQI.
Primary study does not report SOL, TST, WASO, REM or Deep NREM in the tables used here.
MMASH has no smartphone gaming/social media exposure variables comparable to the primary study; datasets must not be joined as if they contain the same people.
The paper reports Bayesian estimates and credible intervals; this repository preserves those rather than calculating bootstrap intervals from aggregate data.
